$description: LinkNMS design tokens — the single source of truth. Edit here; `npm run tokens` regenerates tokens.css (and any other target). W3C Design Tokens format.

owner.$description: Owner Blue — planned / agreed / owner side. Mandatory identity colour. Re-based LINA-86; passes WCAG AA on paper at 6.48:1 (the previous #2a78d6 failed at 4.30:1).

builder.$description: Builder Orange — actual / on-site / builder side. Mandatory identity colour. Re-based LINA-86; 4.20:1 on paper (large text), up from #eb6834 at 3.12:1.

ink.$description: Ink — text and marks. Re-based LINA-86.

paper.$description: Paper — the calm surface. Re-based LINA-86.

surface-sunken.$description: Re-based LINA-92 from #f4f3f0 to the .pen's `ui-sunken`/`paper-sunken`. Warmer, so it sits in the same family as the re-based paper.

muted.$description: Re-based LINA-92 from #5b5b58 to the .pen's `ui-muted-fg`. Cooler — it is a desaturation of the re-based ink rather than a neutral grey.

owner-muted.$description: Re-based LINA-86 — a tint of the re-based owner hue. The old #e2edfb was derived from the retired saturated blue and would not read as the same family.

builder-muted.$description: Re-based LINA-86 — a tint of the re-based builder hue.

success.$description: Re-based LINA-92 from #2e7d54 to the .pen's `ui-success`. This closes the long-standing split with the landing's `--plan-closed` (#2f7d5b) — the two greens are now one value.

warning.$description: Re-based LINA-92 from #b7791f to the .pen's `ui-warning`. Materially darker: the old value was 2.85:1 on paper and could not carry text.

danger.$description: Re-based LINA-92 from #c0392b to the .pen's `ui-danger`. Darker, to clear 4.5:1 as text on paper.

owner-fg.$description: LINA-92. The readable rung of the owner hue — chip text on `owner-muted`, and the owner tone used as body type. The .pen's portal ramp has no `-fg` step, but the portal's retired palette did (`--owner-ink`), so dropping it would regress the party tags. Value reused verbatim from the already-ratified landing token `plan-baseline-fg` rather than invented, since owner and plan-baseline are the same hue.

builder-fg.$description: LINA-92. The readable rung of the builder hue. Required, not optional: `builder` itself is 4.20:1 on paper and 3.44:1 on `builder-muted` — both below 4.5:1 — so builder may never be used as body text or chip text. Reused from the ratified landing token `plan-actual-fg`. Replaces the retired `--builder-ink`.

success-fg.$description: LINA-92. The readable rung of the success hue: `success` on a success tint is 4.05:1 and fails as chip text. Reused from the ratified landing token `plan-closed-fg`. Replaces the retired `--ok-fg`.

line.$description: LINA-92, from the .pen. A hairline lighter than `outline` — table rules and dividers, where `outline` reads too heavy.

line-strong.$description: LINA-92, from the .pen. The visible-divider step between `line` and `outline-strong`.

ink-60.$description: LINA-92 ink alpha ramp, from the .pen. Alpha over an assumed paper backdrop — composite before measuring contrast, never judge in isolation.

ink-45.$description: LINA-92 ink alpha ramp, from the .pen.

ink-35.$description: LINA-92 ink alpha ramp, from the .pen.

ink-25.$description: LINA-92 ink alpha ramp, from the .pen. Below the text threshold on paper — dividers and ornament only.

ink-15.$description: LINA-92 ink alpha ramp, from the .pen (the .pen also calls this `ink-hair`). Hairlines only — never text.

state-warning.$description: LINA-92, from the .pen. Same value as `warning`; the `state-*` ramp is the chip/banner set (fg + muted + line) built around it.

state-warning-fg.$description: LINA-92, from the .pen. Chip text — darker than the base so it clears 4.5:1 on its own tint.

state-warning-line.$description: LINA-92, from the .pen. Chip border — ornament beside text that already contrasts.

state-danger.$description: LINA-92, from the .pen. Same value as `danger`.

state-danger-fg.$description: LINA-92, closing LINA-106 finding 2. The .pen ships warning with four rungs and danger with two; consumers need to address every state the same way. Deliberately EQUAL to `state-danger` rather than a darker invented red: the base tone already measures 5.51:1 on `state-danger-muted`, so unlike warning it needs no separate readable rung. The NAME is what was missing, not the value.

state-danger-line.$description: LINA-92, closing LINA-106 finding 2. Chip/banner border — decorative, beside text that already contrasts. Value promoted from the portal's existing `--bad-bd`, which had never reached the token source.

plan-baseline.$description: LINA-80 plan semantics, promoted into the token source by LINA-87 — the family was specified in the .pen and hard-coded in marketing-site/src/app/landing.css, but had never reached tokens.json, so consumers copied hexes. STATE, not party: the agreed/original commitment. Equal in value to `owner` today, but a separate token on purpose — a change order raised by the builder against an owner-set baseline needs the party and the commitment state coloured independently.

plan-baseline-muted.$description: The empty baseline lane. 1.24:1 on paper — a fill only; it cannot delimit the track by itself, so it must be paired with `plan-track-line`.

plan-baseline-fg.$description: Baseline TYPE, and the fill under white type. 6.95:1 on `plan-baseline-muted`, 8.98:1 under white. Same value as `owner-fg`.

plan-baseline-line.$description: Decorative hairline/chip border only — below the 3:1 non-text floor on paper.

plan-baseline-on-dark.$description: LINA-80 FIX B. Mandatory on a dark field: base `plan-baseline` is 2.62:1 on ink and fails even the 3:1 non-text floor.

plan-actual.$description: STATE: what actually happened — the as-built / as-spent value. Equal to `builder` today, but separate by design (see `plan-baseline`).

plan-actual-fg.$description: LINA-80 FIX D. Actual TYPE, and the fill under white type: 7.11:1 under white, 5.57:1 on `plan-actual-muted`, where the base tone manages only 4.39:1 and 4.20:1. Same value as `builder-fg`.

plan-actual-on-dark.$description: LINA-80 FIX B. Mandatory on a dark field.

plan-closed.$description: STATE: the commitment is settled — agreed, approved, closed out. Same value as `success` after the LINA-92 re-base, but semantically distinct: `success` is RAG health, `plan-closed` is commitment state.

plan-closed-fg.$description: Closed TYPE, and the fill under white type (7.98:1). Same value as `success-fg`.

plan-closed-on-dark.$description: LINA-80 FIX B. Mandatory on a dark field.

plan-track-line.$description: LINA-80 FIX E. The border of an empty plan track. The muted lane fills are ~1.2:1 and cannot delimit the track themselves, so the bar's scale — and therefore the size of any cost or schedule delta read off it — depends on this border being perceivable. Clears 3:1 on paper, stone and cream alike.

lp-ink.$description: Landing ink — the landing page's dark field, same hex as --ink (LINA-108). Kept namespaced so a product engineer knows they are in the landing palette. Landing-scoped: no dark-scheme counterpart (declared in build-tokens.mjs LIGHT_ONLY).

lp-ink-70.$description: Landing ink at 70% — secondary body text on light landing sections.

lp-ink-60.$description: Landing ink at 60% — captions, chip labels on light sections.

lp-ink-40.$description: Landing ink at 40% — right-hand section labels, counters on light sections.

lp-ink-hair.$description: Landing ink at 15% — hairlines and rules on light sections.

lp-cream.$description: Landing cream — the landing page's light field, same hex as --paper (LINA-108). See --lp-ink for the naming rationale.

lp-cream-60.$description: Landing cream at 60% — the minimum tint that clears 4.5:1 on ink. Micro-labels, HUD keys, locale codes, footer links. NEVER set in cream-40.

lp-cream-40.$description: Landing cream at 40% — NON-TEXT ONLY (LINA-108). Dashes, hairlines, decorative rules. As text it fails 4.5:1 on every landing backdrop (worst case 3.15:1).

lp-cream-20.$description: Landing cream at 20% — subtle fills on ink (section rules, hover washes).

lp-cream-hair.$description: Landing cream at 12% — hairlines and card borders on ink (header underline, panel strokes).

lp-stone.$description: Landing stone — warm recessed light surface (thread bubbles, secondary cards).

$comment-color-dark: The dark scheme, ratified by LINA-106 and completed for the plan family by LINA-92. Every key here MUST also exist in `color` — build-tokens.mjs enforces that, so a dark token can never name something the light scheme does not have. The reverse is allowed: light-only tokens (`fade`, the `plan-*-on-dark` rungs) are scheme-specific by nature and are listed as intentionally absent in the build script. This group is emitted into a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block under the SAME variable names as `color`, which is the whole point: a consumer writes `var(--owner)` once and both schemes resolve.

paper.$description: LINA-106. Warm dark base — the brown undertone keeps continuity with the light cream paper. Deliberately lighter than the retired #17170f for contrast headroom.

surface-sunken.$description: LINA-106. Recessed surface — darker than paper, inverting the light scheme's relationship.

surface-raised.$description: LINA-106. Cards and elevation — lighter than paper. In light mode raised is white, i.e. also the highest-luminance surface; the ordering is preserved, the direction is not.

ink.$description: LINA-106. Cream text, the visual inverse of light paper. 15.85:1 on dark paper.

outline.$description: LINA-106. Container borders — 1.52:1, decorative, exactly as in light mode.

outline-strong.$description: LINA-106, corrected by LINA-92. Form-control borders, where the border IS the affordance so WCAG 1.4.11 genuinely applies. LINA-106 set #6a6865 and verified it at 3.17:1 against dark `paper` — but a form control inside a CARD sits on `surface-raised`, where that value measures only 2.83:1 and misses the 3:1 floor. Lightened by the smallest step that clears on all three dark surfaces: 3.05 raised / 3.41 paper / 3.63 sunken. The cost is `ink` on it dropping 5.01 → 4.65:1, still clear of 4.5:1. This is the one place dark is better than light: the light `outline-strong` is 2.76:1 on paper and still fails — an open designer question, and pre-existing, so LINA-92 did not unilaterally move a ratified .pen token to close it.

muted.$description: LINA-106. Secondary text — 6.98:1 on dark paper.

line.$description: LINA-92. Hairline rung, derived as 55% `outline` over `paper` so it sits between paper and outline just as the light `line` does. Decorative only — no WCAG floor applies.

line-strong.$description: LINA-92. Visible-divider rung, derived as 55% `outline-strong` over `paper`. Decorative only.

ink-60.$description: LINA-92. The ink alpha ramp inverts with the scheme — in dark it is CREAM at the same alpha stops, not the light ink. Using the light ramp here would paint near-invisible dark-on-dark.

ink-25.$description: LINA-92 dark ink alpha ramp. Dividers and ornament only.

ink-15.$description: LINA-92 dark ink alpha ramp. Hairlines only — never text.

owner.$description: LINA-106. Owner Blue (dark) — tuned as a FILL: 5.66:1 under white type. Darker than the light owner, because on dark the base tone's job is to be a button background, not type.

owner-muted.$description: LINA-106. Owner tint for party tags.

owner-fg.$description: LINA-106. Owner TYPE (dark) — 9.12:1 on dark paper. The two-tier base/-fg split is the same contract as light mode, but the rungs move in opposite directions: light `-fg` is darker than its base, dark `-fg` is brighter.

builder.$description: LINA-106. Builder Orange (dark) — FILL: 4.68:1 under white type.

builder-muted.$description: LINA-106. Builder tint for party tags.

builder-fg.$description: LINA-106. Builder TYPE (dark) — 9.57:1 on dark paper.

state-warning.$description: LINA-106. Same value as `warning`, mirroring light.

state-warning-fg.$description: LINA-106. Chip text — 8.68:1 on its own tint.

state-danger.$description: LINA-106. Same value as `danger`, mirroring light.

state-danger-fg.$description: LINA-106, closing finding 2. Chip text — 7.59:1 on its own tint.

state-danger-line.$description: LINA-106, closing finding 2. Chip border — decorative.

plan-baseline.$description: LINA-92. The ratified `plan-baseline-on-dark` (LINA-80 FIX B) IS the dark base — on a dark field the -on-dark rung was always the correct tone, and now it is bound to the plain name so consumers stop having to branch. 4.67:1 on dark paper.

plan-baseline-muted.$description: LINA-92. The empty baseline lane, derived as 18% `plan-baseline` over `surface-sunken` — the same 18% recipe globals.css already used, now resolved to a literal so the audit can measure it.

plan-baseline-fg.$description: LINA-92, and the fix for a real dark-mode AA failure. Equal to dark `owner-fg`, exactly as light `plan-baseline-fg` equals light `owner-fg`. REQUIRED: globals.css previously set this to the base #6e85a7, which measures only 3.99:1 on its own tint and failed 1.4.3 for every baseline chip in dark mode. At #a3bce5 it is 7.79:1.

plan-baseline-line.$description: LINA-92. Lane hairline, 40% `plan-baseline` over `surface-sunken`. Decorative only.

plan-actual.$description: LINA-92. The ratified `plan-actual-on-dark`. 4.68:1 on dark paper.

plan-actual-fg.$description: LINA-92. Equal to dark `builder-fg`, mirroring light. Replaces the base tone's failing 4.03:1 on tint with 8.24:1.

plan-closed.$description: LINA-92. The ratified `plan-closed-on-dark`. 4.66:1 on dark paper.

plan-closed-fg.$description: LINA-92. Equal to dark `success-fg`, mirroring light. Replaces the base tone's failing 3.99:1 on tint with 7.50:1.

plan-track-line.$description: LINA-92. The dark counterpart of LINA-80 FIX E — the empty track's border, which is what gives a budget bar its scale. The obvious candidate (dark `outline-strong` #6a6865, and the #6b6a64 globals.css used) measures 2.90:1 on `surface-raised` and misses the 3:1 non-text floor, and the budget bar lives in a card. Lightened until it clears on ALL three dark surfaces: 3.20 raised / 3.58 paper / 3.81 sunken.

sans.$description: The brand's text face. Re-based LINA-86 from the bare system stack to Inter, which the marketing site already self-hosts via next/font. The system stack is retained as the fallback.

display.$description: Landing display face (LINA-80), self-hosted via next/font. Both faces are SIL Open Font Licence — no commercial licence is required.

lp-sans.$description: Landing body face — same stack as --sans, namespaced for the landing palette. The page reads var(--lp-sans, var(--font)).

lp-display.$description: Landing display face (LINA-108) — wordmark 196px, section h2s, HUD figures, money figures. The page reads var(--lp-display, var(--lp-sans, var(--font))).

sharp.$description: Table cells and timeline bars — crisp, drawing-like.
